purpose: A Slicer scripted module that computes fractional myocardial mass (FMM) and myocardial mass at risk (MMAR) by assigning a tetrahedral left-ventricle myocardium mesh to coronary artery centerline segments with a Voronoi/point-interpolation scheme. It targets researchers and clinicians doing coronary physiology analysis who already have centerline trees (e.g. from SlicerVMTK) and a volumetric mesh (e.g. from SegmentMesher).
summary: Small, readable module with no network servers, no pip installs and no environment tampering, but it has a concrete unsafe code path: the sample-data downloader executes a `setup.py` found in a user-chosen folder. The GUI "Apply" path is also broken (segmentMesh returns None but is unpacked into two variables), `qt`/`importlib` are never imported, and the declared SlicerVMTK dependency contradicts `EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA"`. The LICENSE is an unfilled MIT template. Recommend 🔴 Do not merge yet until the arbitrary-code-execution path and the broken Apply path are fixed.

safety.rationale: FMM/FMM.py:51-56 loads and executes a `setup.py` from a folder the user picks in a file dialog; sample data is downloaded without checksums (FMM/FMM.py:80, 99). No telemetry, sockets, pip installs or obfuscation found in the 677-line module.

environment.rationale: No pip_install, no torch, no sys.path or environment changes, no monkey-patching; only vtk/slicer/SampleData imports (FMM/FMM.py:1-8, 65). Heavy imports are inside functions.

packaging.rationale: CMake installs FMM.py plus the icon and .ui (FMM/CMakeLists.txt:5-20) and EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA" matches build_dependencies [], but FMM.py:24 declares SlicerVMTK as a module dependency and a stale FMM/__pycache__/FMM.cpython-39.pyc is committed.

license.rationale: LICENSE contains the MIT text but with the unedited placeholders `Copyright (c) [year] [fullname]` (LICENSE:3), so no copyright holder is identified; no third-party code is bundled.

soundness.rationale: The Apply button path always fails: FMM/FMM.py:324 unpacks two values from segmentMesh, which returns nothing (FMM/FMM.py:505-586). `qt` and `importlib` are used but never imported (FMM/FMM.py:40, 53), registerSampleData is never connected to startupCompleted, and the Voronoi/volume loop runs on the GUI thread without progress.

utility.rationale: README.md documents inputs, outputs and sample data well and a test exists (FMM/FMM.py:593-677), but the test needs SlicerVMTK's ExtractCenterline and downloads data, sample data is not registered at startup, and there is no clinical-use disclaimer.

findings.title: Sample-data downloader executes an arbitrary setup.py from a user-chosen folder
findings.evidence:
filepath=destFolderPath+"/setup.py"
      if (os.path.exists(filepath)):
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("setup",filepath)
        setup = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        spec.loader.exec_module(setup)
findings.explanation: downloadSampleDataInFolder is registered as the customDownloader for the RCA and LCA sample data (FMM/FMM.py:83, 102). When a user loads that sample data (or runs the module test, FMM/FMM.py:618), a folder chooser opens and any file named setup.py in the chosen folder is imported and executed with full Slicer privileges. A user who picks a shared/network folder, a download folder, or a colleague's data folder runs whatever code is there, with no warning and no relation to the module's advertised function. Nothing in the repository ships such a setup.py, so this is dead code that only creates an execution path.
findings.suggestion: Delete the setup.py import/exec block entirely; if post-download setup is genuinely needed, ship it inside the extension and call it directly instead of executing a file from a user-writable directory.

findings.title: Sample data downloaded without integrity checks
findings.explanation: The RCA/LCA markup sources pass checksums=None and the surface/volume sources omit checksums altogether (FMM/FMM.py:85-127), so the .vtp/.stl/.vtu/.mrk.json payloads pulled from the GitHub release are loaded into the scene without verification. Combined with the setup.py execution above, a tampered release asset would be consumed silently.
findings.suggestion: Provide checksums for every registered sample data source.

findings.title: Apply button always fails: segmentMesh returns None but is unpacked
findings.explanation: FMMLogic.segmentMesh (FMM/FMM.py:505-586) has no return statement; it mutates outputModel/outputTable in place. Unpacking its None result raises TypeError, which tryWithErrorDisplay turns into a 'Failed to compute results.' dialog, and the following line 327 then raises NameError on the undefined outputMesh. Every GUI run therefore ends in an error and no display setup (colouring, MMAR table, layout) ever happens.
findings.suggestion: Call segmentMesh without unpacking (or make it return the nodes) and move the display code inside the try block.

findings.title: qt and importlib are used but never imported
findings.explanation: The module imports only logging, os, vtk and slicer (FMM/FMM.py:1-8); `qt` (lines 40, 42) and `importlib` (line 53) are never imported. Any call to downloadSampleDataInFolder raises NameError, so the RCA/LCA sample data and the module test cannot work as written.
findings.suggestion: Add `import qt` and `import importlib` at the top of the module (or remove the code that needs them).

findings.title: Declared SlicerVMTK dependency contradicts EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA"
findings.explanation: CMakeLists.txt:16 sets EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA" and the catalog entry has build_dependencies [], so SlicerVMTK is not installed with this extension, yet the module declares it as a dependency and README.md:51-54 states both SegmentMesher and SlicerVMTK are 'automatically installed'. The module test also imports ExtractCenterline (FMM/FMM.py:614), which only exists with SlicerVMTK, so the test fails on a clean install.
findings.suggestion: Either add SlicerVMTK to EXTENSION_DEPENDS/build_dependencies and the catalog entry, or drop the runtime dependency declaration and correct the README.

findings.title: Stale compiled bytecode committed to the repository
findings.explanation: FMM/__pycache__/FMM.cpython-39.pyc (15 KB, Python 3.9 bytecode) is checked in. It is not installed by CMake (FMM/CMakeLists.txt:5-12 lists only FMM.py and the resources), so it is dead weight that can drift from the source and confuse anyone reading the repository.
findings.suggestion: Remove the __pycache__ directory and add it to .gitignore.

findings.title: LICENSE is an unfilled MIT template
findings.explanation: The MIT grant text is present, so distribution is permitted, but the copyright line still contains the template placeholders, so no licensor is identified and the notice cannot be reproduced as required by the license itself. The sample data published in the GitHub release has no stated license either.
findings.suggestion: Fill in the year and copyright holder (e.g. David Molony) and state the license of the sample data assets.

findings.title: Sample data is never registered at startup
findings.explanation: registerSampleData is only called from the test (FMM/FMM.py:616); there is no `slicer.util.infoDisplay`/`startupCompleted` connection anywhere in the file, so the RCA/LCA/myocardium sample data never appears in the Sample Data module for normal users, contrary to the README's tutorial intent.
findings.suggestion: Connect registerSampleData to slicer.app.startupCompleted as in the module template.

findings.title: MMAR table looked up by hardcoded node name and recreated on every run
findings.explanation: segmentMesh creates a new table node literally named 'MMAR' on each run (FMM/FMM.py:584), and the widget then fetches it by name. After a second run there are several 'MMAR' nodes and getNode may return the wrong (stale) one or raise if the user renamed it; the scene also accumulates duplicate tables.
findings.suggestion: Return the MMAR table node from segmentMesh (or store it in the parameter node) instead of looking it up by name, and reuse an existing node.

findings.title: At-risk points decided by point index rather than position along the vessel
findings.explanation: addMMARArray marks a point as at-risk when its index in the concatenated polydata is >= the index of the closest point to the stenosis marker. Point order in the appended LCA/RCA polydata is an implementation detail of markupToPolyData, so the split between 'proximal' and 'distal' depends on insertion order rather than on arc length along the curve; results can silently be wrong for trees whose points are not ordered root-to-leaf.
findings.suggestion: Compute the arc-length position of each point along its curve and compare with the arc-length position of the MMAR point.

findings.title: Heavy computation on the GUI thread without progress reporting
findings.explanation: The Voronoi point interpolation (FMM/FMM.py:469-486) and the per-cell Python loop in computeVolume (FMM/FMM.py:494-501) run synchronously in the Apply slot with only a wait cursor and a single status message. For the tetrahedral meshes the README recommends, Slicer will appear frozen with no progress or cancel option.
findings.suggestion: Run the computation in a CLI or a worker thread with progress reporting, or at least report progress per cell block.

findings.title: Unguarded display-node access on the input model
findings.explanation: If the selected input model has no display node (e.g. a node created by a script or a CLI output), GetDisplayNode() returns None and this raises AttributeError, aborting the display setup after the mesh has already been computed.
findings.suggestion: Create default display nodes for the input model first, or guard with a None check.

findings.title: README claims dependencies are installed automatically; no clinical disclaimer
findings.evidence: The following extensions are automatically installed with SlicerFractionalMyocardialMass. Although SlicerFractionalMyocardialMass does not directly rely on these extensions, they provide a the capability for generating the required input data.
findings.explanation: EXTENSION_DEPENDS is "NA" (CMakeLists.txt:16), so SegmentMesher and SlicerVMTK are not installed with the extension; users following the README will not find the tools it tells them to use. The README also gives no statement that the computed FMM/MMAR values are research output and not validated for clinical decision making, which matters for a cardiac risk metric.
findings.suggestion: Correct the dependency statement and add a short research-use disclaimer.

findings.title: Test is not registered in the Testing/Python CMakeLists
findings.explanation: The only test is the FMMTest class registered via slicer_add_python_unittest in FMM/CMakeLists.txt:27; the Testing/Python directory is empty apart from a commented-out line. The test itself downloads sample data and needs SlicerVMTK, so it will not pass in a minimal build environment.
findings.suggestion: Either remove the empty Testing directory or add a self-contained test that does not depend on downloaded data.

not_checked: Contents of FMM/__pycache__/FMM.cpython-39.pyc (binary, not readable as text) - could not confirm it matches FMM.py
Contents and license of the sample data assets in the GitHub release (RCA/LCA markups, surfaces, myocardium mesh)
Whether scm_revision "main" currently resolves to the stated commit b8d0559 (reviewed the files provided for that commit)
CI/build results for this extension on the Slicer factory
questions_for_author: Why does downloadSampleDataInFolder execute a setup.py from the folder the user selects? Can that block be removed?
Is SlicerVMTK a real runtime dependency (then EXTENSION_DEPENDS should list it) or only needed for the test?
Should segmentMesh return the output nodes, given the widget unpacks two values from it?
Will you fill in the copyright holder in LICENSE and state the license of the sample data?
